items.author: kirsty.mcfadyen@chairmail.example
items.title: sat - what happened
items.body: full head bleach retouch, 1.5 inch regrowth. mixed Brightline Pro 6% 20 vol 1:2 with Brightline blue powder like always. client said tingly at 10 min, normal for her. 18 min said burning at the crown. rinsed straight away cool water 15+ min. scalp red patch about 2 inch at crown, couple of spots nape. lift was way too fast, she was near pale yellow at 18 min, normally takes 35-40. bottle was new, opened that morning. bought off the Kelvin Trade rep 28 Oct, 4 bottles. checked base of bottle, batch LX2291.

items.author: customercare@kelvintrade-hair.example
items.title: Product Notice: Brightline Pro 6% (20 vol) Cream Developer 1L
items.body:
Dear Customer,

We have been made aware by our manufacturer that a filling error has affected one batch of Brightline Pro 6% (20 vol) Cream Developer 1L. Batch LX2291 may contain 12% (40 vol) developer. The batch code is printed on the base of the bottle. This batch was supplied between 19 October and 5 November 2026.

Please stop using any bottles from batch LX2291 immediately and return them to your rep or to our Hillington depot for a full credit. Other batches and other strengths are not affected.

We apologise for any inconvenience caused.

Kelvin Trade Hair Supplies

items.title: insurance
items.body: Stylesure public liability policy HBX-448120. rang them sat night, ref CL-77310. need photos dated, my notes, the bottle kept (DONT throw out), supplier email. excess £250. they said dont admit fault in writing to anyone.

items.author: gail@studio41.example
items.title: Patch tests and skin tests
items.body: Everyone renting at Studio 41 does a patch test 48 hours before any colour for new clients and anyone who hasn't had colour in 6 months. Write it on their card with the date. Allergy alert test kits are in the back cupboard, top shelf. If someone reacts in the chair, rinse with cool water, no shampoo, and write it in the incident book at the desk. Gail First aid reference for suspected chemical burns: NHS, Acid and chemical burns (https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/acid-and-chemical-burns/). Call 999 for medical help immediately; do not wait for blistering or severe pain. Protect yourself with gloves and carefully remove contaminated clothing if possible. Rinse the affected area with plenty of cool or lukewarm running water for about 1 hour. Do not apply creams or other chemicals. Chemical burns need hospital assessment. Breathing difficulty, throat swelling or collapse also require 999 immediately. Follow the call handler's instructions.
